title: Cold rebuild: What does the command do?
summary: Rebuild What does the command do? from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **What does the command do?** in *Getting out (and saving)*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: You typed `:q` and vim says `E37: No write since last change (add ! to override)`. You want to keep the file as it was on disk. What now?
steps.explain: `!` forces the quit and discards the edits. `:wq` would save the mess you wanted to throw away.
